Depends entirely what you want to use them for.

Flowers? Probably not, unless you want to invest heavily in some climate control to force them to bloom.

Greens? Absolutely. At least in zone 6, you can grow them outside in a semi protected environment like under evergreens or along the south side of a rock wall.

If you are looking for a low maintenance year round source of greens, there are more versatile options. Dandelion will take at least two years to reach harvestable maturity.

A bed of mixed hardy greens like sorrel, burnett, and parsley, along with dandelions, would provide more. Very low maintenance, very hardy, and way more vitamins and minerals than traditional greens.
